requirements.title: Transmitter carrier output power
requirements.description: The transceiver shall deliver 5.0 W (+0.5 W, -1.0 W) A1A carrier power into a 50 Ω load from 144.000 MHz to 148.000 MHz.
requirements.rationale: Why: SI-003 sets 5 W for useful simplex range; NGO-009 (open-ground contact at 5 km) and MOE-001 depend on it; the MOP for MOE-001 is MOP-004, tracked as TPM-015. -1.0 W keeps range within 1 dB of the goal; +0.5 W caps PA dissipation and battery current. Assumes: 50 Ω resistive load, key-down steady state, fresh battery. Ops: OPS-004 paddle QSO, OPS-005 straight-key QSO. KDR: the PA device (ADR-012 sourcing constraint), heat path, battery capacity and enclosure are sized by this value.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (supporting): Analysis case, LTspice .tran of the PA into 50 Ω at 144, 146 and 148 MHz. Post-build (closing Test): Bench on the delivered unit, diode RF probe across the 50 Ω dummy load read on the multimeter, P = Vpk^2 / 100, with the tinySA Ultra through the calibrated attenuator as the secondary reading (04 section 6.2); closing case TC-SYS-001.

requirements.title: Paddle keying speed range and element timing
requirements.description: The transceiver shall time paddle-keyed Morse elements within ±1 % or ±0.5 ms, whichever is larger, of PARIS timing from 5 to 50 WPM.
requirements.rationale: Why: SI-018 (core requirement) calls for a built-in keyer driven by iambic paddles; the functional requirements, one per key type, are separate (02 section 4.6). NGO-013 is the keyer timing objective and MOP-012 its measure (TPM-013); the tolerance is the MOP-012 threshold. 5 WPM lets beginner friends operate (SI-019); 50 WPM is the upper bound the owner accepted in SI-033, recorded by ADR-024. PARIS timing: dit = 1200 / WPM ms. Assumes: the speed is set in the keyer menu (OPS-004).
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (supporting): HostUnit keyer timing test TC-SW-KEYER-003, the closing case of REQ-SW-KEYER-003, at 5, 15, 25 and 50 WPM. Post-build (closing Test): Bench on the delivered unit; paddle closures applied at the key jack; TX_KEY line captured with the Pico-based logic capture (04 section 6.1) at 5, 15, 25 and 50 WPM; element and gap durations compared with PARIS timing; closing case TC-SYS-002.

requirements.title: Transmitter inhibit on over-temperature
requirements.description: The transceiver shall cease RF output within 100 ms after its transmitter temperature exceeds 85 (TBR) °C.
requirements.rationale: Why: control for HZ-003 (power amplifier and enclosure over-temperature and contact burn, docs/safety/hazards.json) under NGO-004 (lawful and safe); OPS-014 is the over-temperature scenario. 85 °C is a best estimate 15 °C below the 100 °C derated case limit of the preliminary thermal budget; 100 ms bounds post-threshold dissipation to about 1 J. Assumes: the sensed temperature is within 5 °C of the hottest transmitter part; the sensing location and the firmware monitor are allocated to TX and SW-SAFE at PDR. Fault tolerance: docs/safety/hazard-analysis.md section 8.1 items 1 and 7; single point candidate 6 of section 8.2. TBR: the PA thermal analysis fixes the threshold.
requirements.verification_note: Pre-build (supporting): HostUnit and Emulation of the thermal monitor. Post-build (closing Test): Bench on the delivered unit; inject the sensor signal at its test pad while keyed into the dummy load; capture key-line and RF-detector output (scaled to a logic level) with the Pico-based logic capture (charter section 9) and measure the inhibit latency against 100 ms; closing case TC-SYS-003.

tbr.owner: Claude prepares the PA thermal analysis; Robin decides
tbr.plan: The PA thermal analysis (docs/design/analysis/, PDR) fixes the inhibit threshold; the value replaces 85 (TBR), the decision is recorded in an ADR and this tbr object is removed in the same CR.
